chapters.CHEM 3A: Ch 6–7 (Introductory Chemistry, Atoms First for FCC)
chapters.CHEM 3B: Intermolecular forces in organic and biological molecules

description: Intermolecular forces, phase changes and colligative properties for CHEM 3A (default), CHEM 1A and CHEM 3B (add ?course=1A or ?course=3B). Seven tiles, shown by course: Spot the Forces (polar or nonpolar, who can hydrogen bond, strongest force, Lewis structure to all the forces, ion–dipole, forces in organic families), Boiling Point Battles (which boils higher and why, rank three, dispersion and shape, organic boiling points, fatty acid melting points), Liquids & Mixing (like dissolves like, surface tension and viscosity, vapor pressure), Phase Changes (name the change, heat in or out, read a heating curve, read a phase diagram), Cells & Osmosis (osmosis, hypotonic/isotonic/hypertonic, osmotic pressure in 1A), Colligative Properties (1A: van’t Hoff factor, concentration units, freezing and boiling points, Raoult’s law) and Biomolecules (3B: amino acid side chains, protein folding, DNA base pairs, carbohydrates, membranes and colloids). Size comparisons show molar mass beside electron count. Every step has a hint. Nine predict-first labs, whose predictions also come up as practice questions with the lab opening under the question: H-Bond Lab, Energy Well, Electron Coin-Flip, Mixing Beaker, Heating Curve Lab, Phase Diagram Explorer, Solutions Lab, Cell Lab and Protein Fold Lab. Learn mode shows Professor Tips and worked examples; Practice gives mistake-specific feedback on every wrong choice; Challenge is 10 mixed questions with no hints; Daily 5 shares the ItsDrDan day streak. Typed answers accept E notation and flag sig figs. XP, ranks, 21 achievements and matched ItsDrDan videos.
